newsitem.title: USA: Girl, 15, killed by "date rape" drug Rohypnol.
newsitem.headline: Girl, 15, killed by "date rape" drug Rohypnol.

text.p: A 15-year-old Texas girl was killed by an overdose of the "date rape" drug Rohypnol at a party last month, police said Thursday.
Thelma Rascon and a friend were given the powerful sedative Rohypnol by five men who then raped the two girls in a downtown El Paso hotel and left them there.

Rohypnol, an odorless and tasteless drug which causes memory loss and unconsciousness, is increasingly being used in sexual attacks and is most commonly slipped into drinks. It is about 10 times stronger than Valium.

Rascon was found dead the following morning and her friend was hospitalized but survived. Police said Thursday that a toxicology report showed the girls had been given Rohypnol, the best known of the rape drugs.

It was the second such death in Texas in recent weeks. A 17-year-old girl last month was killed by an overdose of another drug that was dropped into her drink at a dance club in La Porte, near Houston.
Police said Rascon and her friend were given the drug and took it orally, but did not know what it was. "The girls thought it was just something to get them high," said Detective Millie Hinojos.
Five men have been charged with sexual assault and jailed while awaiting trial, she said.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin earlier this year banned all imports of Rohypnol, but it is easily purchased in Mexico where it costs about 50 cents a pill. On El Paso's streets, the drug sells illegally for about $2.
Rohypnol is made by Hoffman-La Roche, a unit of Roche Holding, and is marketed in South America, Europe and Asia.
